name: Sensor list and vendor metadata
plain: Lists the sensors the phone has, with vendor, resolution and range.
meaning: The set of sensors with vendor and power numbers differs by model and firmware and is a stable device identifier.

limits.headline: Can list the sensors your phone has, with maker, range and precision
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app or game checks what hardware it can use
can: List all sensors on Android, often 20 to 60
See each sensor's maker, resolution and range
Check which sensors exist on iPhone as yes or no answers
Use the list as a clue in a device fingerprint
cannot: Get maker, range and precision details on iPhone; only yes or no answers
See your sensor data from the list itself
limits.differs: Android shows full details. iPhone shows only whether each sensor is available.

story.what_it_is: An app can list your phone's sensors, with maker names and ranges, which differ by model.

marketing.name: Sensors overview
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps list the sensors on a device so they can use what is there.

story.for_you: You do not see it. Apps just check whether your phone has a gyroscope or a heart rate sensor before offering a feature. The list can also single out your model and firmware.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to turn features on or off for each phone. The details, like vendor and range, also form a stable fingerprint of the model. It is more useful to trackers on Android than on iPhone.

use_cases.example: A tilt controlled game checks that you have a gyroscope before it shows motion controls.
An AR app checks for the sensors it needs and tells you if your phone is too old.
A fitness app checks for a step counter and heart rate sensor to decide what to show.
An analytics SDK reads the vendor names and ranges to tell which exact phone model you have.
An anti fraud tool sees a sensor list that looks like an emulator and blocks the sign up.
A developer logs sensor lists in crash reports to find a bug that hits one phone model.

story.android_note: Android apps can list every sensor with vendor, resolution and range with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no public list, but apps can test sensors one by one.
